**Arizona has been taking itself apart since spring; the Rams went all-in and are 2-3 anyway.** Kyler Murray was released and Jacoby Brissett kept the job under first-year head coach Mike LaFleur, a former Sean McVay offensive coordinator. Jeremiyah Love went third overall and Tyler Allgeier came from Atlanta; James Conner (foot) and Trey Benson are on IR, and Marvin Harrison Jr. was told he was inactive before Week 5 while a trade was finished (one report says Houston: verify).
- **Arizona is 1-4** (26-14 at the Chargers, then losses of 31-7, 36-30, 36-24 and 45-21), 21.6 points scored and 32.4 allowed a game. The line is patched: Paris Johnson Jr., Isaiah Adams and Chase Bisontis are on IR, so Jayden Williams, Jon Gaines II and Elijah Wilkinson start.
- **The Rams sent Jared Verse and three picks to Cleveland for Myles Garrett,** who had knee surgery after Week 1 and is still on IR. Aaron Donald came out of retirement, and Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson came over from Kansas City. Matthew Stafford is the reigning MVP.
- **Los Angeles is 2-3** (119 points for, 120 against) after a 37-34 overtime loss to Buffalo on Monday: Harrison Mevis missed two field goals, one blocked in overtime, and the Rams signed K Blake Grupe on Tuesday (verify who kicks). LT Alaric Jackson is suspended for this game, so David Quessenberry starts, and the Rams play on a short week.

**The NFL's top passing offense draws its worst pass defense, and Arizona plays without the back it built around.** Arizona has allowed 21 touchdowns in five games (most in the league), a 117.3 opponent passer rating (worst), 252.4 passing yards a game and touchdowns on 76.5% of red-zone trips. Through Week 4 it had given up eight touchdowns and 10.6 yards a target to receivers, and Gibbs ran for 151 and two scores last week. Two safeties are out and Budda Baker is questionable.
- **Rams offense:** 433.8 yards a game and the league's most passing yards, but only 23.8 points because of six Stafford interceptions and a 65% red-zone rate. Kyren Williams (70-343-4, 33 targets, 13 red-zone carries through Week 4) gets the goal-line work. Davante Adams has 4 touchdowns on 45 targets, but with Puka Nacua active he has 12 catches for 109 in three games. Nacua caught 17 of 24 for 138 on Monday. Higbee has had 11, 6 and 6 targets, and Parkinson's return brings back three-tight-end sets.
- **Arizona offense:** Brissett is 132 of 199 at 5.6 a throw with 9 touchdowns and 5 interceptions. McBride has 56 targets and 3 scores, from the 3, the 2 and the 9; Wilson has 51 targets. Bourne (8), Brooks (7) and Virgil (5) took over Harrison's role in Week 5, and Quitoriano scored twice from in close. With Love out, Allgeier and Bam Knight get the carries and Brissett keeps the sneaks.
- **Rams defense:** 165 passing yards a game allowed. Through Week 4 it allowed 4.8 an attempt, held tight ends to 12 of 29 for 85 and gave up no touchdowns to backs on 87 carries. Buffalo pushed the rushing yards allowed to 128.4 a game. Garrett is out, Byron Young has 3.5 sacks, and McDuffie (groin) is questionable.

**Both teams run through a backup plan on Sunday: Tyler Huntley for Baltimore, a depleted backfield for Cleveland.** Baltimore is 4-1 under first-year head coach Jesse Minter (Declan Doyle calls the offense): 41-23 at Indianapolis, 17-24 to New Orleans, 34-31 over Dallas, 24-18 over Tennessee and 30-23 in overtime at Atlanta with Huntley. Lamar Jackson (ankle) is out for the second straight week.
- **Baltimore's moves:** Trey Hendrickson (four years, about $112 million) missed Weeks 4 and 5 after finger surgery and was a full participant this week with no designation. Center Cam Jurgens, acquired from Philadelphia on Oct 7, is out again (concussion). TE Durham Smythe is on IR and TE Matt Hibner is out, so Josh Cuevas and Nick Vannett back up Mark Andrews. Rookie WR Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) was activated from IR Saturday and is questionable.
- **Cleveland is 3-2 under Todd Monken** (34-10 loss at Jacksonville, three one-score wins, then 12-17 at the Jets on a season-low 198 yards). Deshaun Watson has started every game after missing 2025: 95 of 148, 1,010 yards, 7 touchdowns, 2 interceptions; Shedeur Sanders is the backup and Dillon Gabriel is on IR. Myles Garrett was traded to the Rams in the offseason (desk's Week 5 notes).
- **The Browns' backfield is down to its third and fourth options behind a hurt starter:** Raheim Sanders (hip) went to IR Tuesday, Dylan Sampson (knee) was not activated, Audric Estime was signed Tuesday, and Jaleel McLaughlin (2 carries, 31 yards, a touchdown) is up from the practice squad. Quinshon Judkins (ankle) is questionable.
- **The receiving tree is two rookies and a second-year tight end:** KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston (16 catches, 330 yards, 3 touchdowns) and Harold Fannin Jr.; Jerry Jeudy has 15 targets in five games.
sections.matchup:
**Derrick Henry against a Cleveland interior without its three rotation tackles decides the game.** Mason Graham (team-high 4 sacks) is not expected to play (Plain Dealer), Mike Hall Jr. is out and Kalia Davis is on IR. Cleveland allows about 4.5 a carry and 117.4 rushing yards a game and ranks 29th in EPA per rush over Weeks 2-5; Baltimore's run game is 6th and 3rd in yards (164.4). Henry has 113 carries for 476 yards and 7 rushing touchdowns, and had 11 of the Ravens' 13 carries inside the 5 through Week 4.
- **Cleveland's red zone is the counterweight:** touchdowns on 42.9% of trips, second in the league (Squawka), and no rushing touchdown allowed until Braelon Allen's 22-yarder in Week 5.
- **Huntley's tree at Atlanta:** 24 of 32 for 201, two touchdowns, 3 of 4 in the red zone. Targets: Flowers 9, Bateman 6, Andrews 6, Hill 4. Scores went to Henry (18-yard catch), Devontez Walker (7) and Huntley (a 1-yard sneak). Cleveland allows 239.8 passing yards a game, 8.8 yards per target to receivers and three tight-end touchdowns on 36 tight-end targets through Week 4.
- **Cleveland scores through Fannin and Boston:** Fannin from the 2, the 14 and the 2 (two of the team's three targets inside the 5); Boston from 46, 55 and again at the Jets, but 0 for 3 inside the 20. Judkins is 73 carries for 221 (3.0) with one touchdown.
- **Pressure:** the Browns' line has allowed 19 sacks, most in the league, with G Teven Jenkins out again; Hendrickson returns to a defense in the top 10 in EPA over the last two weeks. Baltimore allows 102 rushing and 238 passing yards a game.
- 60F, dry, gusts to 18 mph on the lakefront.

sections.offseason:
**Chicago gets its quarterback back after three games and loses half its front seven in the same week.** Ben Johnson's second Bears team is 3-2: 59-37 at Carolina and a 3-9 home loss to Minnesota with Caleb Williams, then 27-7 over Philadelphia (Case Keenum), 23-12 over the Jets and 31-7 at Green Bay (Tyson Bagent, with Keenum in relief). Williams tore his right hamstring on Sep 20, practiced fully all week, and ESPN and NFL Network report he starts.
- **DJ Moore was traded to Buffalo in March** for a second-round pick, so Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Kalif Raymond are the top three receivers and Colston Loveland is the move tight end; rookies Sam Roush (TE) and Zavion Thomas (WR) are on the two-deep. Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) is out for the second straight week, and D'Andre Swift leads Roschon Johnson in the backfield.
- **The defense lost four front-seven players in a week:** Montez Sweat was suspended two games (performance-enhancing substances) on Tuesday, Dayo Odeyingbo went to IR (quad), and linebackers T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Keyshaun Elliott (quad) are out. Safety Anthony Johnson Jr. is out, Xavier Woods (two starts at safety) was released Saturday and Nick McCloud was signed; nickel Kyler Gordon was activated from PUP for his 2026 debut on a limited snap count, per coordinator Dennis Allen.
- **Atlanta rebuilt under Kevin Stefanski** after Raheem Morris and GM Terry Fontenot were fired (Ian Cunningham is GM). Cooper Rush started the first two games (13 and 3 points); Michael Penix Jr., back from the torn ACL that ended his 2025, is 2-1 as the starter (35-14 at Green Bay, 45-24 at New Orleans, 23-30 in overtime against Baltimore). He hurt his ribs against the Ravens, Tua Tagovailoa threw three passes in relief, and Penix has no designation this week.
- **Atlanta's other moves:** Brian Robinson Jr. signed a one-year deal to back up Bijan Robinson after Tyler Allgeier left for Arizona. On defense Jalon Walker (ACL) is out for the season, James Pearce Jr. is suspended into November (verify the date) and A.J. Terrell Jr. is on IR, so Za'Darius Smith, Samson Ebukam and Cameron Thomas were added to the rush.
sections.matchup:
**Atlanta's run game against a Chicago front without Sweat, Odeyingbo, Edwards and Elliott decides this.** The Falcons hand off more than any team (Covers): 33 runs a game, and Bijan Robinson has 102 carries for 580 (5.7). Eight of their 11 touchdowns since Penix took over were runs. Chicago allows 4.3 a carry to backs and is 27th in EPA per rush allowed, and those numbers came with the four absent players on the field.
- **Atlanta's goal line:** Bijan has 7 of the team's 8 running-back carries inside the 5 and 20 red-zone carries (scores from the 3, 2 and 4, plus a 59-yard run and a 23-yard catch). Brian Robinson Jr. has 5 red-zone carries and four touchdowns from the 7, 4, 8 and 11. Atlanta is 9 of 13 in the red zone, all of it with Penix.
- **Drake London has not been targeted inside the 25 all season:** 37 targets, 27 catches, 488 yards, no touchdowns. Atlanta's red-zone throws are spread: Kyle Pitts Sr., Jahan Dotson and Bijan two each, Austin Hooper, Olamide Zaccheaus, Charlie Woerner and Brian Robinson Jr. one each; Hooper and Pitts both scored from the 5.
- **Chicago's pass defense gives up the big play:** 8.8 yards an attempt, 16.0 yards a catch to receivers, and four of the five receiver touchdowns it has allowed went 42 yards or longer (Jalen Coker 51, Isaiah Williams 58, Christian Watson 42 and 53). Jordan Love had six completions of 25-plus last week. Tight ends have 18 catches on 27 targets and no touchdowns against Chicago.
- **Chicago with Williams:** 36 of 55 for 407 yards in his two games, plus 15 runs for 107 and two scrambling touchdowns in Week 1. Swift has 9 of the Bears' 19 carries inside the 5 and Monangai (out) had 6, so the goal line is Swift's; Roschon Johnson had 5 carries and 7 targets in the one game without Monangai. Red-zone targets: Burden 8, Loveland 6, Raymond 4, Odunze 4. The Bears are 9 of 21 in the red zone.
- **Atlanta's defense:** 6.2 yards an attempt allowed, 11 sacks, the league lead in quarterback hits (Covers), and 5.1 yards a catch to backs. But Baltimore ran 35 times for 208 last week, the secondary is without C.J. Henderson (out) and Terrell (IR), and tight ends catch 73% of their targets against it (three touchdowns).
- **Pressure:** Chicago allowed four sacks at Green Bay, and Williams plays his first game since the hamstring tear against the league's top quarterback-hit rate.

**Houston spent a 2027 second-round pick on a receiver at 1-4; Jacksonville is 4-1 and has not left London.** The Texans went 12-5 and reached the divisional round for the third straight year in 2025, traded for David Montgomery (from Detroit) and signed Reed Blankenship, then lost their first four by 5, 14, 2 and 4 before a 26-3 win at Tennessee. DeMeco Ryans took the defensive play-calling back from Matt Burke before that win.
- **The Harrison trade (Oct. 12):** Houston sent 2027 second- and seventh-round picks to Arizona for Marvin Harrison Jr. and a 2027 sixth. The No. 4 pick of 2024 had 5 catches on 13 targets for 85 yards and a touchdown in four Cardinals games (41-608-4 in 2025) and reunites with C.J. Stroud, his Ohio State quarterback in 2021-22. He passed his physical Monday, practiced Wednesday, and Ryans says he plays but not all 60 snaps.
- **Houston's depth chart moved again:** Tank Dell (knee) is still on IR with his practice window open and did not travel, Jayden Higgins is on IR, and Jared Wayne was waived (claimed by Miami). Montgomery (groin) is out, so second-year back Woody Marks starts. Stroud has no interceptions in 186 attempts.
- **Jacksonville is in year two under Liam Coen** after a 13-4 season (franchise best) and a wild-card loss to Buffalo. Daniel Faalele and Ameer Abdullah were added, Coen leans on 12 personnel, and Travis Hunter has played every defensive snap the last two weeks with five offensive snaps in Week 5. A win makes the Jaguars 5-1 for the first time since 1999.
- **London, part two:** the Jaguars beat the Eagles 19-17 at Tottenham on Cam Little's 57-yard field goal and stayed in England (Anton Harrison's knee surgery is set for when the team returns); the Texans landed Friday morning. Lawrence has a touchdown pass in all eight of his London starts (5-3).
- **Series:** Houston leads 32-16 and won the last meeting 36-29 on Nov. 9, 2025, rallying from 19 down in the fourth quarter with Davis Mills; Jacksonville then won its last eight regular-season games.

Through the air it is different: 266.2 passing yards a game (third most), 9.5 yards per receiver target, the league's worst explosive-pass rate (17.2%) and 76% completions on in-breakers (ESPN), and CB Montaric Brown is out.
- **Collins is built for that:** 25 targets, 3 red-zone targets and 3 touchdowns (12, 7, 22 yards) in his three games, five straight 100-yard games against Jacksonville, and 41% of Stroud's throws are in-breakers. Harrison debuts on a partial share; Noel works the slot, so Harrison's snaps come from Hutchinson (31% in Week 4) and Boutte.
- **Goal line without Montgomery:** he had 9 red-zone carries and 3 of Houston's 6 carries inside the 5. Marks has 8, 5 inside the 10, scores from the 1 and 6, and ran 15 times once Montgomery left Week 5. Jacksonville allows touchdowns on 5 of 16 red-zone trips and 2 of 8 back carries inside the 5 scored. Backs catch 5.8 passes a game against it (35 targets).
- **Tight ends:** Schultz has 3 red-zone targets and no score, with 2 and 4 targets since Collins returned; Moreau has Houston's tight-end score (from the 1). Two of the seven touchdowns Jacksonville has allowed went to tight ends.
- **Jacksonville's offense:** Lawrence is 96 of 143, 1,174 yards, 10 touchdowns, 3 picks on 23 to 39 attempts; 9 of 14 in the red zone. Tuten has 82 carries, 12 in the red zone, 3 inside the 5 and both scores from the 1; Rodriguez has 6 red-zone carries but two carries last week. Washington leads with 35 targets and 5 red-zone looks (4 TDs, 3 from 27+ yards), Strange has 16 targets in two weeks, and Meyers and Cameron have 4 red-zone targets and 2 scores each.

Receivers have its six passing touchdowns, tight ends none, backs 2.9 yards a target. **Final reports (Oct 15-16) and Saturday moves.** Texans **Out:** RB David Montgomery (groin) and S Jalen Pitre (shoulder), both hurt at Tennessee; WR Tank Dell (knee) remains on IR and did not travel. LB Henry To'oTo'o (shoulder) and CB Ja'Marcus Ingram (elbow) are **Questionable** and were activated from IR Saturday (LB Aiden Fisher and CB Collin Wright waived); LB E.J. Speed is listed Out. RT Braden Smith was reinstated from IR Wednesday. Marvin Harrison Jr. carries no designation and will play on a limited snap count.
- **Jaguars:** CB Montaric Brown (hamstring) and LS Ross Matiscik (shoulder) **Out**; CB Devon Marshall is **Questionable** on ESPN's feed (Field Level Media lists a Jaylon Jones, hamstring: verify). LT Anton Harrison (knee) went to IR Tuesday and Walker Little starts. S Eric Murray (concussion) and TE Nate Boerkircher (back) have no designation. LS Jacob Bobenmoyer was signed to the practice squad (elevation: verify). DE Bryan Thomas Jr. was ejected in Week 5; no suspension was reported (verify).
- **Where Houston's touches go:** Montgomery's 10.4 carries a game and his 3 carries inside the 5 go to Marks first (15 carries for 62 yards in Week 5 after the injury) and Dare Ogunbowale second. Jawhar Jordan is priced at both books but is on the practice squad and had not been elevated in ESPN's transaction log at 21:50 UTC Saturday (verify at inactives). Montgomery's 1.4 targets a game go to Marks. Harrison takes outside snaps from Hutchinson and Boutte; Noel's slot role holds. Wayne's 12 targets are gone with him to Miami.
